$comment: Coldline Task 2.7 benchmark report contract. The harness writes one report per measured arm and both are retained: .benchmark/baseline.json and .benchmark/experiment.json. The assessed checks grade the recorded answers against these retained reports rather than against a fresh measurement, so this contract is what makes a report gradeable at all. It validates shape, identifiers, and provenance. It cannot authenticate a wall-clock measurement, and nothing here claims to: the identifier and consistency checks establish that a report describes this template, these fixtures, and that configuration, not that the timings in it were observed.
title: Coldline Task 2.7 benchmark arm report
description: One retrieval configuration measured against the golden evaluation set, with the provenance needed to grade an answer against it.

report_schema_version.description: Version of this contract the report was written against. A report from an older harness is invalid rather than silently accepted.

harness_version.description: Version of the measurement procedure: warmup count, repeats per query, and percentile rule. A change to any of them makes reports incomparable, so it changes this number.

template_id.description: Which Task template produced this report. Read from the supplied config/benchmark-template.yaml, never from the environment.

fixture_id.description: Digest over the exact golden evaluation set the arm ran against, so two arms can be shown to have been measured against identical fixtures.

configuration_id.description: Digest over the arm's own validated retrieval configuration. Recomputed from `config` by the checks, so a report cannot claim a configuration it did not measure.

run_id.description: Identifier of the capture that produced this report. The two retained reports must carry different run identifiers: a single capture cannot have measured both arms and still be two independently retained runs.

captured_at.description: UTC timestamp of the capture, in RFC 3339 form with a trailing Z.

arm.description: Which side of the comparison this report is. The baseline arm must have measured the supplied baseline configuration.

config.description: The retrieval configuration measured, as validated by the harness.

golden_set_digest.description: Same value as `fixture_id`, kept under the harness's own name so the printed report and the contract read alike.

query_ids.description: Every published golden query measured, in published order.

failed_query_ids.description: Queries whose measurement failed. A report with any entry here is not a valid basis for a decision.

recall_at_k.description: Mean deterministic Recall@K over the measured queries. Recomputed from `queries` by the checks.

judge_relevance.description: Mean cached-judge relevance over the measured queries. Comparison evidence only; it takes no part in the adoption rule.

judge_faithfulness.description: Mean cached-judge faithfulness. Comparison evidence only.

latency_p50_ms.description: Median query latency in milliseconds. Present so that recording the median where the p95 was asked for is a detectable mistake rather than an invisible one.

latency_p95_ms.description: 95th-percentile query latency in milliseconds, nearest-rank over every sample from every query. This is the figure the answer sheet and the adoption rule both use.

latency_samples.description: How many timed requests the percentiles were taken over, warmup excluded.

queries.description: Per-query outcomes. The aggregate metrics are recomputed from these, so a report whose totals disagree with its own rows is invalid.
